Search speeches for words and phrases

Source: R/query-search.R
search_speeches_by_terms.Rd

Returns the turns whose text contains the given terms, one row per turn, with the number of exact occurrences (n_hits) and a BM25 relevance score (score). It takes the same filters as get_speeches() and returns the same columns plus score and n_hits. Counts by year or by speaker are aggregations over this result; see the examples.

Usage

search_speeches_by_terms(
  terms,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  member = NULL,
  party = NULL,
  parliament_id = NULL,
  chamber = NULL,
  chamber_venue = NULL,
  type = c("speech", "question", "answer"),
  include_presiding = FALSE,
  exact = TRUE,
  conjunctive = TRUE,
  include_text = TRUE,
  columns = NULL,
  collect = TRUE,
  limit = NULL
)

Arguments

terms

A character vector of words or phrases, such as c("LGBT", "same-sex marriage").

from, to

Sitting-date bounds, inclusive: a year (covering the whole year), a Date, or a "YYYY-MM-DD" string. NULL leaves that end open.

member

Character vector of member PHIDs. A PHID that matches no member is an error; look one up with find_member().

party

Party ids (numbers) or party names or abbreviations (strings); see Details.

parliament_id

Filter on the sitting's parliament_id: a vector of values or in_range().

chamber

"house" and/or "senate", in any case.

chamber_venue

Filter on the turn's chamber_venue: a vector of values or in_range().

type

Turn types to return: any of "speech", "question", "answer" and "interjection". Defaults to all but "interjection".

include_presiding

If TRUE, also return presiding-officer turns.

exact

If TRUE (the default), verify every match exactly and count n_hits. If FALSE, return the index's stemmed matches with n_hits = NA.

conjunctive

If TRUE (the default), a turn must contain every term; if FALSE, any term.

include_text

If TRUE (the default), add the content column. Results with content are held to the lower size ceiling, getOption("ausparl.max_rows_text").

columns

Character vector of columns to return; NULL returns all.

collect

If TRUE (the default), return a tibble; if FALSE, a lazy table for further dplyr work.

limit

Maximum number of rows to return, or NULL for no limit.

Value

A tibble with one row per matching turn and the columns of get_speeches() (content when include_text = TRUE), plus score (BM25 relevance, NA for a regex scan) and n_hits (exact occurrences of all terms, NA when exact = FALSE). Rows are ordered by score, highest first. Zero rows if nothing matches. With collect = FALSE, an unordered lazy table, so it can be aggregated inside DuckDB.

Details

Two-stage matching. With exact = TRUE (the default):

  1. Recall. The database's full-text index (fts_main_actions, BM25) finds candidate turns within the years of from and to. Each term is split into words the way the index splits text (lowercased, accents and punctuation removed, digits dropped) and stopwords such as "the" or "same" are dropped, so "same-sex marriage" searches for sex and marriage. The index stems words, so this stage finds more turns than match exactly.

  2. Verification. Each candidate's content is checked with a case-insensitive regular expression built from the term. Regex special characters are matched literally (so "LGBTIQ+" and "C++" mean exactly that), whitespace inside a phrase matches any run of whitespace, and a term must start and end at a word boundary wherever its first or last character is a letter, digit or underscore. n_hits is the total number of occurrences of all terms in the turn.

With conjunctive = TRUE a turn must contain every term; with FALSE, at least one.

Terms with no indexed words. If a term has no words left once stopwords and digits are dropped (for example "the" or "1996"), the index cannot help, so the whole search scans content with the regular expressions alone, within the other filters. This is slower; a one-line message says so, and score is NA.

exact = FALSE. Returns the index's candidates only: stemmed matches ("tariff" also finds "tariffs"), without the regex check, and n_hits is NA.

Turn types (B1) and filters. As in get_speeches(): interjections are left out unless type includes "interjection", and presiding-officer turns unless include_presiding = TRUE.

Requirements. Search needs the database's full-text index and the DuckDB fts extension. If the database has no index (fts_main_actions), the call fails with an ausparl_db_error: use the official released build of the database; ausparl never builds the index. If the fts extension cannot be loaded, the call fails with an ausparl_db_error saying how to install it. There is no fallback to a full regex scan in either case.

Words with a soft hyphen. The index splits words at every number, punctuation mark, symbol and space (so "budget—you" gives budget and you), but a word that contains a soft hyphen (U+00AD, usually invisible) stays one token, so the recall stage does not find its parts on their own.

See also

get_speeches(), find_member()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
# Search needs the DuckDB fts extension, installed once with network access.
if (isTRUE(db_info()$fts_available)) {
  search_speeches_by_terms("immigration", include_text = FALSE)
  search_speeches_by_terms(c("foreign affairs", "Indonesia"),
    from = 2002, to = 2002,
    columns = c("action_id", "date", "name_raw", "n_hits")
  )

  # Counts are aggregations over the lazy result.
  hits <- search_speeches_by_terms("government", include_text = FALSE, collect = FALSE)
  hits |>
    dplyr::summarise(n_turns = dplyr::n(), n_occurrences = sum(n_hits)) |>
    dplyr::collect()
  hits |>
    dplyr::group_by(year = year(date)) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n_turns = dplyr::n(), n_occurrences = sum(n_hits)) |>
    dplyr::collect()
}
